   \[
   6 \times 6 = 36

   - \(7^2 \equiv 4 \mod 5\)
   - \(7^3 \equiv 3 \mod 5\)
   - \(7^4 \equiv 1 \mod 5\)

2. Notice that \(7^4 \equiv 1 \mod 5\). This means that every fourth power of 7 will be congruent to 1 modulo 5.

   - \(2026 = 4 \times 506 + 2\)
